speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start with your history: when did your neck and arm pain first begin, and did it follow any specific injury or repetitive activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That history of burning pain and progressive weakness over a year sounds very concerning for cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy, possibly related to the prior motor vehicle accident. Given your age and diabetes, I need to check if there is any numbness in your groin or saddle area, and have you lost any bowel or bladder control?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spinal Stenosis (likely with myelopathy)
